messages.text: Jones warns England: You were good vs Japan, but All Blacks will be 'violent'

metadata.summary: Former England head coach Eddie Jones praised his old side as "very good" as they tore his Japan apart 78-15 on Saturday, but warned the All Blacks will be "violent" against them next week.
metadata.content: Eddie Jones warns England: You were very good against my Japan, but All Blacks will be 'violent' next week after Wales loss | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Eddie Jones warns England: You were very good against my Japan, but All Blacks will be 'violent' next week after Wales loss Eddie Jones warns England the All Blacks will be 'violent' at Twickenham next week; Will Joseph scored five as England registered 13 tries in huge Nations Championship victory, with Jones' Japan alarmingly inferior; Steve Borthwick admits he now has 'thinking' to do around selection Michael Cantillon Sports Journalist Saturday 14 November 2026 20:41, UK Image: Former England head coach Eddie Jones threw a warning their way ahead of the All Blacks visiting Twickenham next week Former England head coach Eddie Jones praised his old side as "very good" as they tore his Japan apart 78-15 on Saturday, but warned the All Blacks will be "violent" against them next week. Following South Africa's defeat to France in Paris on Friday, victory for New Zealand against Wales in Cardiff would have seen them claim World Rugby's No 1 ranking, and take charge of the Nations Championship southern hemisphere table. Instead, the All Blacks suffered their first defeat to Wales since 1953 in a shock 35-28 loss up against an immense Welsh defensive effort, and next play England at Twickenham next Saturday. Sent off the heavily backed 2-1 favourite on his first run since winning as a novice at the Festival in March, he put in some tremendous leaps on the way round for Harry Cobden. messages.text: Tandy hails 'phenomenal' Wales players after historic win

metadata.summary: Steve Tandy hailed his "phenomenal" players after Wales delivered a stunning performance to sink New Zealand 35-28 in the Nations Championship in Cardiff.
metadata.content: Nations Championship - Wales 35-28 New Zealand: Steve Tandy hails 'phenomenal' players after historic win over All Blacks | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Nations Championship - Wales 35-28 New Zealand: Steve Tandy hails 'phenomenal' players after historic win over All Blacks Steve Tandy branded his players "phenomenal" after their historic Nations Championship win over New Zealand; Wales beat All Blacks for first time in 73 years, ending run of 34 successive defeats Saturday 14 November 2026 19:28, UK Image: Wales ended a run of 34 consecutive losses against the All Blacks Steve Tandy hailed his "phenomenal" players after Wales delivered a stunning performance to sink New Zealand 35-28 in the Nations Championship in Cardiff. It was the first time since 1953 that Wales could celebrate beating the All Blacks, ending a run of 34 successive defeats in one of world rugby's historically most one-sided fixtures. On three separate occasions Wales led by 14 points, and for the first time they scored five tries against New Zealand, but ultimately it was heroic defensive work that denied the visitors. They were boxing over 10 rounds in a non-title bout at a catchweight of 165lbs, but for the unheralded Warburton it was a step up into a whole new class. The Briton seemed almost surprised that he managed to go deep into the fight and celebrated going the distance at the end of their fight in Riyadh. Adames began tamely himself, restrained in his offensive output but Warburton did even less. The Welsh southpaw backpedalled as Adames trudged forward and looked to land single shots. After three quiet rounds, Adames brought in more pressure, forcing Warburton towards the ropes. The Briton grew busier with his jab but Adames was hunting him down. The England head coach said before Croatia at Wembley on Thursday that he was quite happy to go full-strength in both matches, despite the three-day gap, and he was true to his word. All the big guns were out for Harry Kane's big night. Barring unexpected late injury or illness, the best player in the world will lead the line against the world champions. Morgan Rogers should start at right wing, Anthony Gordon left wing. England's Madrid maestro Jude Bellingham will play No 10, and Elliot Anderson and Declan Rice will form the double pivot.
